clue.text: Chicken gives two cries of pain

parts.note: a yell is a loud cry, here one of pain
ow is the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: A bird squawks twice as if it has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two cries of pain' gives two pieces, YELL and OW. 'Chicken' is not the bird here; it is the adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal adjectives for cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: Young racehorse, indeed, left in enclosure

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed

indicators.note: in puts the left letter inside the enclosure

parts.note: a ring is an enclosure, as at a racecourse or circus

explanation.surface: A young racehorse is indeed left in its paddock.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse in its second year, between one and two years old, is a young racer.

clue.text: Apprentice gets some money with lucrative job

parts.note: L stands for pound (from Latin libra), a sum of money
an earner is something that brings in money, as in a nice little earner

explanation.surface: A trainee is paid money for a well-paid post.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice still being taught a trade is a trainee.

clue.text: Spectators see all right, surrounded by remarkable people

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first pieces sit inside the remarkable people

parts.note: a oner is an exceptional person, one of a kind
lo is an old word meaning look or see
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Watchers check that all is well, ringed by outstanding people.
explanation.definitionFit: People who watch something without taking part are bystanders, spectators.

clue.text: I'm usually inside old garb I redesigned

indicators.note: clothing that is redesigned is remade in a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes refashioning an old outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the voice of the answer: a habitual prisoner who says he is usually inside, meaning in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual criminal spends most of his time in prison, so he could say he is usually locked up.

clue.text: Writer could make you relax, amused and diverted

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside, so these letters are sent in a new order

explanation.surface: An author's books could make you relax, entertained and amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make you' is a link phrase. Alexandre Dumas was the French author of The Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist, author of The Count of Monte Cristo.

clue.text: Look menacingly at inferior

definitions.meaning: to lour or glower is to frown threateningly
lesser or ... in rank or position

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to frown darkly and lesser in status or place.

clue.text: I raced with man from Perth and one from Tehran

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, raced
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name, and Perth is a city in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone recounts racing with a Scot and a Persian.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, not the Australian one; IAN is the Scottish form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital of Iran, so a person from there is a native of that country.

clue.text: Conflict with daughter in case that judge overturned

parts.note: if means on condition that or in case that

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down light the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: Someone clashes with their daughter over a case a judge reversed on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case that' reads as part of a legal case, but gives IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree or clash with someone is to be in conflict.

clue.text: Destitute and ragged, someone's banned

indicators.note: ragged means torn and tattered, so these letters are torn apart and reset

explanation.surface: A poor, shabby person has been barred from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; the 's of someone's is just S in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means hard up, in desperate financial straits, as a ship lying on its side is in peril.

clue.text: A bit of children's play to open in theatre immediately

parts.note: tag is a chasing game played by children
a surgeon lances a boil, cutting it open, in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: A scene from a children's show opens a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but here it is the operating theatre, where a surgeon will lance (cut open) a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at first sight means doing it instantly, with no delay.

clue.text: Dock — dock flower

indicators.note: to dock is to cut short, so the last letter of the river's name is cut off

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river; the Wharfe is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A plant called dock is being named as a kind of flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'dock' looks like the weed of that name, but it is the verb meaning cut short. 'flower' is the crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing place where ships tie up to load and unload is a quay or dockside.

clue.text: President's kind of green

definitions.meaning: Abraham ... was the sixteenth US president
... green is the bright green cloth associated with Robin Hood

explanation.surface: A leader's favourite shade of green is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was a US president, and Lincoln green is a named shade of woollen cloth.

clue.text: Cockney's very fine travel company

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: a hairline crack or line is extremely thin

explanation.surface: An East Londoner praises a holiday firm as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very fine' reads as praise but means extremely thin, like a hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier that flies passengers on scheduled routes is a firm in the travel business.

clue.text: Tender rail workers attached to steam engine originally

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A tender, the coal wagon, is coupled to a locomotive by railway staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like the wagon behind a steam engine; it is the verb meaning to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient or look after someone carefully is to care for them.

clue.text: Deposit small sum in foreign currency with head of treasury

indicators.note: in puts the small sum inside the foreign currency

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and Malaysia
a dime is the US ten-cent coin, a trifling amount

indicators.note: head of points to the opening letter of the word treasury

explanation.surface: Someone banks a little money in an overseas currency with the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' reads as banking money but is the noun for matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles out of a liquid and collects at the bottom is a deposit.

clue.text: Bleak time, note, with Rebecca's husband out East

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: out means the compass letter is removed

parts.note: Maxim de Winter is the husband in Daphne du Maurier's novel Rebecca

explanation.surface: A dark period comes when the husband in Rebecca is away in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' means the compass letter leaves the husband's name. Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's novel; its heroine marries Maxim de Winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth of the cold season, around the solstice, is a bleak time of year.

clue.text: Youngster brewing green tea

indicators.note: tea that is brewing is stewing in the pot, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A young person is making a pot of green tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen is a youngster, an adolescent.

clue.text: A merger's organised in Cumbrian village

indicators.note: a merger that is organised is arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company merger is being set up in a northern English village.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASMERE is a village in the Lake District, in the county of Cumbria in north-west England, home of the poet Wordsworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasmere is a village in the Cumbrian Lake District, known for Wordsworth's Dove Cottage.

clue.text: Engineers assume responsibility for rally

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to cover for a colleague is to take on their duties

explanation.surface: Army engineers take charge of a car rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' looks like a motor race but is the verb meaning get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally after illness or a setback is to regain strength, to get better.

clue.text: Famous Elizabethan duke, a libertine

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man of loose morals

explanation.surface: A notorious Tudor nobleman is said to have been a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was an English sea captain under Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake, the navigator who sailed round the world, served Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Expunge a mistake involving oil I spilt

indicators.note: involving means the mistake wraps round the next piece

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

indicators.note: spilt means the letter has been spilled out of the word oil

explanation.surface: Someone tries to wipe out a blunder after spilling some oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I spilt' means the letter I is spilled out of the oil, and 'involving' puts what is left inside the slang blunder. BISH is British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge something is to wipe it out entirely, to do away with it.

clue.text: Mate hitched up sagging skin

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces read from the bottom upward, backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend, a mate
to get hitched is to marry, to wed

explanation.surface: A partner has just married someone with loose folds of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run PALWED, making DEWLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose fold of flesh hanging from the throat of cattle or people is sagging skin.

clue.text: Cry out without need

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, used to mean without as in ex dividend
a claim is a demand, something one needs or is owed

explanation.surface: Someone shouts although nothing requires it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout suddenly in surprise or emotion is to call out.

clue.text: Bill has free bitter

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to rid someone of something is to free them of it

explanation.surface: An invoice comes with a complimentary bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like a pub beer but is the adjective for a sharp taste or smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, pungent taste or smell is harsh, bitter.

clue.text: Fabulous creature from university taking care of sailors

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university
c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A mythical beast is sent from a university to look after seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word joining UNI to CO and RN; 'Fabulous' means from fable, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a single horn is a beast of legend, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Celebrate about prize for Americans

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates winning an award in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is the US spelling of prise, to force open with a bar; it reads as an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Prising something open with a bar uses leverage, so the verb means force apart.

clue.text: Discovering uranium's missing -— almost a disaster

indicators.note: missing means the element's symbol is left out

parts.note: unearthing something is digging it up, discovering it
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Finding that uranium has gone astray nearly causes a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in uranium's means is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call, where calamity was narrowly avoided, is almost a disaster.

clue.text: March around one's garden

indicators.note: around means the march encloses the next piece

parts.note: to parade is to march in procession
one is I, and the 's is S, giving IS

explanation.surface: A procession goes round a person's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' stands for the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden, the first garden in Genesis, is heaven on earth.

clue.text: Dan Cupid?

definitions.meaning: Dan is the farmer at the head of the family in the long-running BBC radio soap set in the village of Ambridge
Cupid, the Roman god of love, shoots arrows from a bow

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one name, but it is two definitions: Dan is a character in a famous BBC radio serial, and Cupid is a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan is the family patriarch in a BBC radio soap, and Cupid is a bowman who fires love darts.
